title: Separated finite-type spaces have separated finite-presentation closed envelopes
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact; a morphism is quasi-compact when its pullback by any affine scheme has quasi-compact source. A morphism is quasi-separated when its diagonal is quasi-compact. A closed immersion is representable and is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Local finite type and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation. Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space and let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type. There exist an algebraic space $Z$, a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow Z$, and a separated morphism of finite presentation $g:Z\to Y$ such that $g\circ i=f$.

proof.text: The finite-type hypothesis makes $f$ quasi-compact for affine tests and locally of finite type. First compare conventions. Let $a:A\to B$ be quasi-compact for affine tests and let $C\to B$ be a map from a quasi-compact space. By [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests], $a$ is quasi-compact for quasi-compact scheme tests. Choose a quasi-compact scheme $U$ with a surjective etale $U\to C$; then $A_U=A\times_BU$ is quasi-compact, so choose a quasi-compact scheme $T$ with a surjective etale $T\to A_U$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $A_U=(A\times_BC)\times_CU\to A\times_BC$ is surjective etale, and for every scheme $V\to A\times_BC$ the base changes $V_U=V\times_{A\times_BC}A_U$ and $V_U\times_{A_U}T\cong V\times_{A\times_BC}T$ are schemes, surjective etale over $V$ and over $V_U$ respectively. Their composite is surjective etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition]. So $T\to A\times_BC$ is a representable surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme, and $A\times_BC$ is quasi-compact. Conversely an affine scheme is a quasi-compact space through its identity atlas [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Hence the affine-test convention of the statement agrees with the quasi-compact-space-test convention of the nodes cited below. With $C=Y$ and the identity, $X=X\times_YY$ is quasi-compact. The diagonal of $f$ is a closed immersion by separatedness; [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper] makes it proper, hence quasi-compact, so $f$ is quasi-separated. Apply [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] to $f$ and the quasi-separated space $Y$ (its absolute diagonal is the diagonal of $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$) to conclude that $X$ is quasi-separated.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-fp-envelope] to the locally finite-type map $f$ between the now verified qcqs spaces $X,Y$. Obtain $j:X\hookrightarrow W$ and $h:W\to Y$ with $h$ finitely presented and $hj=f$. By [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source], $W$ is qcqs. This stage need not be separated over $Y$.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-fp-approximation] to $j$. It gives a small nonempty directed system $W_a\hookrightarrow W$ of finitely presented closed subspaces, closed immersion transitions, and closed immersions $q_a:X\hookrightarrow W_a$, with limit $X$ over $W$. It is also the limit over $Y$: a compatible cone has a common composite to $W$ (directedness gives a common later index for any two indices), so its unique factorization over $W$ is its unique factorization over $Y$. Each transition is affine: after an affine scheme test, the closed-immersion characterization [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies its source with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$. Each $W_a$ is qcqs by [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source], applied over $W$. The composite $g_a:W_a\to W\to Y$ is finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. The compatibility in the approximation gives $g_aq_a=f$.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-fixed-base-eventually-separated] to $(W_a\to Y)$: the base is quasi-separated, all stages are qcqs, transitions are affine, and its limit map is the given separated $f$. Choose an index $a$ in the resulting tail. Set $Z=W_a$, $i=q_a$, and $g=g_a$. The preceding step supplies the closed immersion, finite presentation and equality $gi=f$, while the chosen tail supplies separatedness of $g$.
